description: The line plot illustrates the performance of different query selection strategies for Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) on the MS-Marco dev set, measured by MRR@10, as the number of queries used during inference (S) increases from 1 to 10. The x-axis, labeled “Number of queries used during inference (S),” is linearly scaled with integer tick marks at 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. The y-axis, labeled “MRR@10,” ranges from 33.0 to 36.5 with tick marks at 0.5 intervals. Six strategies are compared, each represented by a solid line (corpus expansion during inference) and a corresponding dotted line (typical representation), except for “DPR w/o query,” which has no dotted counterpart. The “DPR w/o query” (black solid line) starts at approximately 33.0 and remains flat across all S values. “DPR w/ gold” (yellow solid line) begins at 33.0, rises steadily to 35.0 at S=10, with its dotted counterpart starting at 34.5 and rising to 35.0. “DPR w/ top-1” (green solid line) starts at 34.8, increases to 36.4 at S=10; its dotted line begins at 34.5 and remains flat. “DPR w/ bottom-1” (purple solid line) starts at 34.8, slightly dips to 34.7 at S=6, then rises to 34.9 at S=10; its dotted line starts at 34.8 and stays flat. “DPR w/ random” (blue solid line) starts at 34.8, rises slightly to 35.7 at S=10; its dotted line starts at 34.8 and remains flat. “DPR w/ curriculum” (red solid line) begins at 35.5, peaks at 36.0 at S=6, then stabilizes near 36.0; its dotted line remains constant at 35.5. All solid lines show improvement or stability with increasing S, while dotted lines (except “DPR w/ gold”) are mostly flat, indicating that corpus expansion during inference enhances performance relative to standard representation.
